title: Enrichment analysis with perturbation signatures
text: Signatures available human ("hsa") mouse ("mmu"). file downloaded cached. Rows can named gene symbol Entrez ID; use gene symbols match microarray annotation . column one signature, include one several perturbations (megered together couldn’t reliably distinguished). Weights signed: positive weights mark genes go perturbation negative weights mark genes go . gene-related signatures, positive direction corresponds -regulated genes gene-activating perturbations (e.g., overexpression) -regulated gene-inhibiting perturbations (e.g., gene knockout).
code: signatures <- loadSignatures("hsa", geneId = "symbol") dim(signatures) #> [1] 9733  165 head(colnames(signatures), 10) #>  [1] "12_O_TETRADECANOYLPHORBOL_13_ACETATE" #>  [2] "17_BETA_ESTRADIOL"                    #>  [3] "1_25_DIHYDROXYVITAMIN_D3"             #>  [4] "2_3_7_8_TETRACHLORODIBENZO_P_DIOXIN"  #>  [5] "2_DEOXY_D_GLUCOSE"                    #>  [6] "4_HYDROXYTAMOXIFEN"                   #>  [7] "4_THIOURIDINE"                        #>  [8] "5_AZA_2_DEOXYCYTIDINE"                #>  [9] "5_AZACYTIDINE"                        #> [10] "5_FLUOROURACIL" weights <- signatures[, "IFNG"] topSets <- getGeneSets(signatures[, "IFNG", drop = FALSE], topK = 10, direction = "both") topGenes <- data.frame(gene = unlist(topSets), weight = weights[unlist(topSets)])  ggplot(data.frame(weight = weights), aes(weight)) +     geom_histogram(bins = 100) +     geom_point(data = topGenes, aes(x = weight, y = 1), colour = "firebrick") +     ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = topGenes, aes(x = weight, y = 1, label = gene),                              size = 3, nudge_y = 1, direction = "both",                              max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0) +     scale_y_continuous(transform = "log1p", breaks = c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000)) +     labs(title = "IFNG signature weights", x = "Weight", y = "Genes (log scale)")

title: Enrichment analysis with perturbation signatures
text: GSE41291 microarray time course HSG cell line, untreated treated IFN-alpha IFN-gamma, triplicate. use 4-hour samples make two DE comparisons: IFN-alpha vs untreated IFN-gamma vs untreated. fgsea needs one statistic per gene, fitting drop probes without unique gene symbol, keep highly expressed probe gene, keep 12,000 highly expressed genes:
code: gse <- getGEO("GSE41291", AnnotGPL = TRUE)[[1]] gse$condition <- sub("^HSG (\\S+) .*$", "\\1", gse$title) gse$time <- sub("^HSG \\S+ (\\S+) rep\\d+$", "\\1", gse$title) gse4hr <- gse[, gse$time == "4hr"]  table(gse4hr$condition) #>  #>  IFNalpha  IFNgamma untreated  #>         3         3         3 symbols <- fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol` gse4hr <- gse4hr[!is.na(symbols) & symbols != "" & !grepl("///", symbols, fixed = TRUE), ] gse4hr <- gse4hr[order(rowMeans(exprs(gse4hr)), decreasing = TRUE), ] gse4hr <- gse4hr[!duplicated(fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol`), ]  gse4hr <- gse4hr[seq_len(min(12000, nrow(gse4hr))), ] featureNames(gse4hr) <- fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol` dim(gse4hr) #> Features  Samples  #>    12000        9

title: Enrichment analysis with perturbation signatures
text: rank genes limma t-statistic. fit$t one column per contrast, genes row names:
code: condition <- factor(gse4hr$condition, levels = c("untreated", "IFNalpha", "IFNgamma")) design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition) colnames(design) <- levels(condition)  contrasts <- makeContrasts(IFNalpha = IFNalpha - untreated,                            IFNgamma = IFNgamma - untreated,                            levels = design) fit <- lmFit(gse4hr, design) fit <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts)) ranks <- list(IFNalpha = fit$t[, "IFNalpha"],               IFNgamma = fit$t[, "IFNgamma"]) lengths(ranks) #> IFNalpha IFNgamma  #>    12000    12000

title: Enrichment analysis with perturbation signatures
text: getGeneSets() takes topK genes largest weights signature, genes go perturbation. Use direction = "" genes go , direction = "" (_UP _DN sets). Passing genes DE profile universe picks top genes among fgsea can use, every gene set keeps topK genes. comparisons come arrays, share one gene universe. positive NES means DE profile goes way perturbation; negative NES means goes opposite way.
code: geneSets <- getGeneSets(signatures, topK = 100, universe = names(ranks$IFNalpha)) length(geneSets) #> [1] 165

title: Enrichment analysis with perturbation signatures
code: set.seed(42) fgseaRes <- lapply(ranks, function(stats) {     fgsea(pathways = geneSets, stats = stats) }) plotTopSignatures <- function(fgseaRes, stats) {     topUp <- fgseaRes[ES > 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]     topDown <- fgseaRes[ES < 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]     plotGseaTable(geneSets[c(topUp, rev(topDown))], stats, fgseaRes, gseaParam = 0.5) }

title: Convert signatures to gene sets — getGeneSets
text: signatures Signature weight matrix (genes x signatures), returned loadSignatures(). topK Number genes per gene set. direction "" (top weights) "" (bottom weights) make one set per signature, named signature; "" makes two sets per signature, named _UP _DN suffixes. universe Genes choose , example names statistic vector gene sets tested . Restricting keeps every gene set topK genes fgsea drops genes missing statistic.

title: Load perturbation signatures — loadSignatures
text: Reads perturbation signatures (per-gene logistic regression coefficients) human mouse. TSV file downloaded https://zenodo.org/records/23986547/ first call read cache afterwards.

title: Load perturbation signatures — loadSignatures
code: loadSignatures(   species = c("hsa", "mmu"),   geneId = c("symbol", "entrez"),   cacheDir = tools::R_user_dir("pertsig", which = "cache"),   force = FALSE )

title: Load perturbation signatures — loadSignatures
text: species Species code: "hsa" (human) "mmu" (mouse). geneId Gene identifiers use row names: "symbol" "entrez". identifier occurs , first row kept. cacheDir Directory downloaded files cached. force TRUE, download file even cached.

title: Load perturbation signatures — loadSignatures
text: numeric matrix signature weights genes rows signatures columns. Signatures merge several perturbations named first one ("IFNG + STAT1" becomes "IFNG").
